title: Compass: Encrypted Semantic Search with High Accuracy
problem: Semantic search systems cannot efficiently support similarity queries over encrypted embeddings because standard encryption schemes do not allow direct comparison operations on encrypted data. Existing approaches face a tradeoff between encryption overhead, query latency, and search accuracy degradation.
motivation: Privacy-preserving semantic search enables applications to perform intelligent search on sensitive data such as medical records, legal documents, and personal information without exposing raw data to service providers.
method: Compass combines homomorphic or functional encryption schemes with approximate nearest neighbor search to enable encrypted similarity queries on embedding vectors. The system uses selective quantization and dimensionality reduction to reduce the computational cost of encrypted operations while preserving search accuracy. Query execution leverages secure comparison protocols that maintain semantic similarity relationships without full decryption.
key_novelty: An encrypted semantic search scheme that achieves high accuracy through encryption-aware approximate search techniques and optimized vector quantization that minimizes the accuracy-privacy-performance tradeoff.
contributions: End-to-end encrypted semantic search system with practical efficiency
Novel technique for maintaining search accuracy under encryption constraints
Demonstration of accuracy preservation compared to unencrypted baselines
Evaluation on real-world semantic search workloads

metrics.accuracy: search precision and recall on encrypted queries
